power.cc: CC1 (A5) and CC2 (B5) each through their own 5.1 k to GND (R1, R2): USB-C sink advertisement.
power.usb_data: D+ (A6/B6) and D- (A7/B7) through U2 USBLC6-2SC6 to GPIO20/GPIO19 (DevKitC J3-19/J3-20): the rear port flashes and talks to the ESP32-S3 native USB. The DevKitC 'USB' micro port shares the same pins, so only one of the two may be connected at a time (physical check still needed for the stub).

devkit_isolation.finding: On the DevKitC-1 v1.1 schematic (SCH_ESP32-S3-DevKitC-1_V1.1_20221130.pdf) each micro-USB VBUS reaches the VCC_5V net through its own Schottky diode (D1 and D7, 1N5819HW-7-F). The header 5V pin (J1-21) is VCC_5V, which feeds the SGM2212-3.3 LDO.
devkit_isolation.consequence: Backplane +5V into J1-21 cannot back-feed a PC on the DevKitC's own USB ports: those diodes block it. If someone powers only from a DevKitC USB port, about VBUS - 0.4 V reaches the backplane +5V and the rear USB-C VBUS pins.
devkit_isolation.decision: No series diode between F1 and +5V. A Schottky would drop about 0.4-0.5 V at 1-1.5 A and push the Catalex microSD module (4.5-5.5 V) out of range. Factory rule: never connect the DevKitC USB and the rear USB-C at the same time; flash through the rear USB-C. Fit a low-drop ideal-diode stage in a later revision if the factory needs both ports at once.

cartridge.keepout_why: top: board 8.0 + tallest envelope 20.0 (PH plug + wire bend, estimate) rounded up with margin; bottom: board underside minus 1.5 mm for through-hole pin ends. Below that only the 4 bosses reach the floor.

antenna_keepout.rule: no metal (screws, inserts, magnets, speaker, metal paint) within 15 mm of the antenna; plastic wall only. 15 mm is from secondary sources (library rows 01/12); verify against the WROOM-1 datasheet.

cartridge.placement_rule: Board lies flat (rotation 0: board +x = world +X, board +y = world +Y). Board centre x = world x 0. Board slides as far toward the rear (+Y) as the inner shell allows: the J_PWR front face sits 0.2 mm inside the inner rear wall surface, and the whole keep-out box keeps clearance_mm to every inner wall. With a rear cover the rear bosses (board y 75.1, OD 7.2) also stay 0.8 mm forward of the cover seam: y_off + 75.1 + 3.6 + 0.8 <= seam_y (silhouette seam_y = depth/2 - min(edge_round, 6) - 1.5); the CAD then cuts the 13 x 7 plug tunnel from the outer surface to the receptacle face. Base plate: floor = 3.5. World point = (bx - W/2, by + y_offset, floor_z + 6.4 + bz). gstudio.normalize writes the chosen board_origin into spec.derived.cartridge.
cartridge.factory_access: DevKitC micro-USB ports face +X (robot's left) for bench flashing before the cartridge goes in; production flashing uses the rear USB-C (native USB on GPIO19/20) or the bottom test pads TP1..TP7.
